newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty urges release of Suu Kyi aide in Burma.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges release of Suu Kyi aide in Burma.

text.p: Amnesty International called on Wednesday for the release of a top official in Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party who has been detained by Burma's military government.

Kyi Maung, deputy chairman of the NLD and one of Suu Kyi's closest confidants, was detained for questioning by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) on Tuesday, diplomats and party sources said .
Amnesty said Kyi Maung had done nothing more than call for peaceful political change.

"His arrest is an outrage and he should be released immediately. This arrest is part of a relentless attempt by the Myanmar (Burmese) authorities to crush any peaceful dissent by whatever means," the London-based human rights organisation said in a statement.
Amnesty said it was concerned about reports of arrests of students during recent demonstrations.
Kyi Maung, 75, was in Rangoon's infamous Insein Prison from 1990 to 1995 for his role in the democracy movement.

The SLORC on Wednesday accused him of colluding with some students involved in an early-morning protest. They said he was helping politicise a scuffle between students and restaurant owners and trying to create unrest by staging a protest.
On Wednesday about 500 Burmese university students staged a rare demonstration against the military government and its detention of three classmates involved in the scuffle.
Kyi Maung gave speeches to supporters along with Suu Kyi at the front gate of the Nobel Peace laureate's house on Sunday.
The government has regularly attacked Kyi Maung through official media, saying he was trying to undermine the peace and stability of the nation.
